whatItIs.text: Young onions pulled before the bulb swells — milder and sweeter than mature onions, with edible tops and white base; the Welsh onion variety never bulbs at all.

historyNote.text: The name traces to the ancient port of Ascalon in the eastern Mediterranean — scallion and shallot both descend from Ascalonian onion. In Chinese cooking, scallion with ginger and garlic is called the holy trinity.

howToChoose.text: Look for perky green tops and crisp white bulbs without sliminess; the thinner they are, the milder they tend to be.

storage.text: Stand roots-down in a jar of water, loosely covered, in the fridge; they regrow from the white base too. The rulebook has the timing.

foodSafetyRef.note: fresh-vegetable windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Chop the greens into everything — eggs, noodles, marinades — or make scallion oil by gently cooking them in oil; the whites char beautifully under a hot grill.

substitutions.note: similar mild onion top-note; less crunch
sharper and sweeter; soak in water 10 minutes to tame
